ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
There are several identical small steel balls released from a certain position on an inclined plane every 0.1 seconds without initial velocity. After releasing several small steel balls continuously, a photograph is taken of the several small steel balls rolling on the inclined plane, as shown in the figure. It is measured that $AB = 15\mathrm{cm}$ and $BC = 20\mathrm{cm}$. The photograph has a 1:1 scale relationship with the actual object.

1. The velocity of ball B when taking the photo.
2. There are several small steel balls rolling on top of ball A.

After releasing several small steel balls continuously, a photograph is taken of the several small steel balls rolling on the inclined plane, as shown in the figure. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is an inclined plane rising upward to the right; if moving downward along the inclined plane, the direction is toward the lower left. The small balls are distributed in sequence on the inclined plane; the labeled A is on the relatively upper right, B is on the lower left of A, and C is on the lower left of B, so A, B, and C may be regarded as three consecutive positions corresponding to adjacent release intervals; B was released earlier than A and is positioned lower, and C was released even earlier than B and is positioned lower. In the figure, on the upper right of A there are also small ball positions continuing closer to the release end. Reasoning: The release time interval of adjacent small balls is Δt=0.1 s, and the photo is 1:1, so AB=0.15 m and BC=0.20 m. The small balls are released from rest from the same position and make uniformly accelerated motion on the inclined plane; the increase of consecutive adjacent spacings satisfies BC−AB=a(Δt)^2. Therefore a=(0.20−0.15)/(0.1)^2=0.05/0.01=5 m/s^2. Let the time for which ball B has already moved at the time of taking the photo be t_B, then AB is the distance between B and A, which was released 0.1 s later than it: AB=aΔt(t_B−Δt/2). Equivalently, v_B=a t_B=AB/Δt+(aΔt)/2=0.15/0.1+(5×0.1)/2=1.5+0.25=1.75 m/s. From v_B=a t_B, obtain t_B=1.75/5=0.35 s, so the motion time of ball A is t_A=t_B−0.1=0.25 s. After A, small balls will still be released every 0.1 s, so at the time of taking the photo, the subsequent small balls above A have ages of 0.15 s and 0.05 s respectively, 2 in total.
